_README: THREE DRAFTED ROWS extending the scan benchmark past its German-publisher
monoculture. Kept OUT of works.json on purpose: scan_eval REFUSES to report a
pooled figure while any scored row is `first_pass`, so merging an unverified
row would break the gate for every session, not just this one. Promote a row
into works.json only after its `check` list is confirmed against the print.
WHY THESE WORKS AND NOT THE ONES ASKED FOR. The request was Universal/Mahler 1,
Novello/Elgar 1 and Durand/La mer. None can be a row: the library holds an
edition PDF for each and ZERO reference encodings, and this harness scores
against truth. Of the 27 works pairing a PDF with truth, every one is
German-published except three, and these are they.
The Tchaikovsky pair is better than a third work would have been: Jurgenson and
Heugel print the SAME MUSIC, so a publisher effect is measured against a
control instead of confounded with repertoire.
⚠️ The training set covers Universal, Novello and Durand; this benchmark cannot
validate those traditions directly. That gap is unavoidable given the library
and should be stated wherever the gate result is quoted.
Each window was established by TWO independent witnesses, as the harness
requires — a barline count off the ink, and the reference's activity grid
compared to the printed page. They fail differently: the count cannot be fooled
by an encoding difference, the grid cannot be fooled by a column of ink.
What is NOT yet done is a human confirming the page starts where the row says.

rows.label: Tchaikovsky 4 / Heugel Paris 1961 / FRENCH engraving, movement opening

window.established_by: movement opening — the page prints the title, 'I' and 'Andante sostenuto', so first_ref_measure is 1 by construction rather than by inference
verified_by: barline count: probe_page_measures over 11 tacet-ish bands gives 5 measures on 8 of them, at a shared barline x-set. The 3 disagreements are explained and benign — band 2 adds two columns at x 558/643 (its own clef and key signature, header ink) and band 9 (Timpani) finds only one column.

activity grid: verify_window over measures 1-5 predicts sound in Bassoon 1-2 and Horn 1-4 only, with Trombone 3 entering for ONE note in m5 and everything else silent. The printed page matches on all 24 parts, including the discriminating detail — the '3 e Tuba' staff carries its only figure at the far right of the last bar, and the winds and all five string staves are empty across the page.
check: confirm the page's first printed bar is the movement's bar 1 (no pickup)
confirm the page holds exactly 5 measures

rows.label: Tchaikovsky 4 / P. Jurgenson Moscow / RUSSIAN engraving — same music as the Heugel row, publisher-controlled

window.established_by: movement opening — the page prints 'СИМФОНІЯ № 4 / SYMPHONIE N° 4', 'I.' and 'Andante sostenuto'
verified_by: barline count: read off the page's whole-measure rests — Flauto I prints 6 of them. ⚠️ probe_page_measures could NOT corroborate this row: its band finder returns 5 bands on a 16-staff page, so the automated count is unavailable here and the number is hand-read.

activity grid: verify_window over measures 1-6 predicts Bassoons and Horns sounding throughout, Trombone 3 alone for one note in m5, and Trombones 1-2 + Tuba ENTERING in m6. The printed page matches — both trombone staves are empty until the final bar and carry ff figures there, and the winds and strings are silent across the page. This is discriminating in both directions: at 5 measures the trombone entry would not appear, at 7 the flutes and oboes would.
check: confirm the page's first printed bar is the movement's bar 1
confirm the page holds exactly 6 measures (Flauto I shows 6 whole-bar rests)
the band finder failed here — a human count is the ONLY ink-side witness

rows.label: Holst, Mars / Goodwin & Tabb London 1921 / ENGLISH engraving, pocket score, 29 staves incl. one-line percussion

edition.publisher_as_catalogued: Goodwin & Tabb, London, 1921 (Hawkes Pocket Scores reissue, B.& H.15970)

window.established_by: movement opening — the page prints 'I. Mars, the Bringer of War' and 'Allegro'
verified_by: barline count: probe_page_measures gives 5 measures on the majority of bands at an IDENTICAL barline x-set across them (664, 1273, 1772, 2268, 2765, 3272). The disagreements are at the ends only — a band that misses the final barline reads 4, and one that picks up the brace column at x 423 reads 6; no band disputes the shared interior positions.

activity grid: verify_window over measures 1-5 predicts the ostinato sounding continuously in Timpani 1, Tam-tam, both Harps and all five string groups, with Bassoons 1-2, Contrabassoon and Horns 5-6 entering at m3 and Bass Oboe at m5. The printed page matches, including the col legno strings and the two harp staves running throughout.
check: confirm the page's first printed bar is the movement's bar 1
confirm the page holds exactly 5 measures

⚠️ 64 reference parts against 29 printed staves — heavy condensation (2 Piccolos share a staff, 3 Clarinets share a staff). Like the Mahler row, this needs `staves_as_printed` rather than a parts map, and FIVE of its staves are ONE-LINE percussion a five-line detector cannot find. Until that map is hand-built the row should report OMR-NED only.
